steps: Identify the initial teams, permissions and sandboxes for the rollout.
Create or verify the roles and check each team can access the correct sandbox.
Map the licensed channels to the first use cases and record the required channel settings.
deliverables: Channel plan for the initial use cases
asks: Administrator access and a list of teams and licensed channels
risk: Shared access can expose work in the wrong sandbox. Test permissions as a representative user from each team.
outcome: Each team can reach the right sandbox and knows which channels are in scope.

steps: Confirm the sending subdomain, consent fields and sender settings with the email team.
Configure the subdomain, IP pool and email channel settings for the approved use case.
Validate sender details, headers and suppression behavior with an approved test profile.
asks: Licensed email channel and DNS owner
Approved sender settings and test profiles
risk: A sending identity or suppression gap can affect deliverability. Verify the approved settings before the first send.
outcome: The email team can send through a tested channel configuration that uses the approved sender and suppression settings.

steps: Agree the audiences, messages and timing for the initial scheduled campaigns.
Configure each campaign with the agreed audience, channel, content and schedule.
Run proof and audience checks with test profiles and document the publication settings.
asks: Approved campaign content and target audiences
risk: A scheduled campaign can reach the wrong audience. Validate audience membership and test profiles before publishing.
outcome: The marketing team can run the initial scheduled campaigns from reviewed audiences and channel settings.

steps: Agree which audience or profile event starts each supported journey.
Configure the entry, action and test profile data for each agreed journey.
Validate entry, action and exit behavior with representative profile-level tests.
deliverables: Journey entry and exit test results
asks: Agreed audiences or profile events and test profiles
risk: A broad audience can admit unintended profiles. Test the entry rules with profiles that should qualify and profiles that should not.
outcome: The first journeys can start from approved audiences or supported profile-level entry conditions.

steps: List the groups that need access and map each group to its product profile.
Set up the users and groups in Adobe Admin Console and link the product profiles.
Test membership and sample access as users from each agreed group.
asks: Adobe Admin Console access and approved user groups
risk: Group assignments can grant more access than needed. Test both permitted and restricted actions using sample accounts.
outcome: Asset teams can sign in with the correct permissions for the agreed environment.

steps: List the required standard renditions and the upload folders that need them.
Configure the supported processing profiles and apply them to the agreed folders.
Upload sample assets and verify the output renditions meet the agreed dimensions and formats.
asks: Agreed upload folders and sample assets
risk: An incorrect folder assignment can generate unwanted renditions. Validate each profile against a sample upload before rollout.
outcome: Asset teams receive the required standard renditions for uploads to the agreed folders.

steps: Check the deployment inventory and applicable service packs with the platform owner.
Validate applicable service packs and configuration changes in the test environment.
Coordinate production installation, review logs and rerun the agreed smoke tests.
asks: Deployment inventory and access to a test environment
risk: A service pack can affect existing integrations. Test critical pages and authoring before and after installation.
outcome: The operating team has a repeatable path to validate and install the applicable service packs.

steps: Inventory the AEM installation, runtime dependencies, content and custom code.
Prepare the test environment and rehearse the upgrade on a representative copy.
Resolve agreed compatibility issues and validate authoring, publishing, integrations and the upgraded code.
Agree the production cutover, backup, rollback and ownership with operations.
asks: AEM environment access and a representative test copy
risk: Custom code or runtime dependencies can block an upgrade. Rehearse the steps and agree recovery before production.
outcome: The site team has a validated upgrade and a repeatable production cutover to AEM 6.5 LTS.

steps: Confirm the author, publish and delivery endpoints and identify critical paths.
Complete the test plan for authoring, publishing and representative page requests.
Document production checks, approvals and the recovery plan with the operations team.
asks: Test environment and production operations owner
risk: Publishing and public page delivery can fail independently. Test both before approving the cutover.
outcome: The operations team can release the AEM 6.5 site using a validated sequence and recovery plan.

steps: Identify the users, access roles and starting audience use cases.
Assign Target permissions and configure the agreed environments and reporting settings.
Build the initial audiences and verify access and audience conditions with test users.
asks: Admin Console access and the approved Target user roster
risk: Overbroad access and audience rules can affect experiments. Verify each role and audience before launch.
outcome: The experiment team has the core users, environments and audiences for the first tests.

steps: Agree the lead fields, scoring signals and sales handoff requirements.
Configure the initial scoring and data cleanup programs and document the treatment of missing values.
Test scoring and handoff against representative leads and confirm the results with sales.
deliverables: Lead scoring program and field rules
asks: Sample lead data and approved scoring rules
risk: Unexpected field values can route leads incorrectly. Test edge cases before handing the scoring program to operations.
outcome: Marketing can score leads consistently and verify their handoff to the sales team.

steps: Confirm the sandbox entitlement, test data and integration boundaries.
Set up representative programs and isolated test data in the sandbox.
Run program and handoff tests, then record approved steps for production configuration.
asks: Licensed sandbox and approved test data
risk: Test records can reach production when systems share a connection. Verify environment separation before running tests.
outcome: Marketing can verify the agreed changes in a sandbox before configuring production.

steps: Identify the source and target environments and the objects approved for promotion.
Build an environment promotion package and check its object dependencies.
Install the package in the agreed test environment and review the installation record.
asks: Workfront sandbox access and approved object list
risk: A package can include unintended objects. Agree the inventory and validate the package before moving it to production.
outcome: The Workfront team can promote the agreed objects with a tested package and recorded validation.

steps: Collect the field labels and tooltips that need translation and agree the scope with team owners.
Configure the approved translations for the selected terms and languages.
Verify the localized labels using representative accounts and hand over an update guide.
asks: Approved translations and representative user accounts
risk: Labels can differ from the teams’ working terms. Review sample forms in each agreed language before rollout.
outcome: Team members see the approved custom field labels and tooltips in their configured language.

steps: Agree the reporting use case and the approved tool, users and network addresses.
Create the reader account and reporting connection and configure the approved allowlist.
Validate sample queries and document connection ownership and credential rotation.
asks: Workfront Data Connect entitlement and reporting tool access
risk: An overly broad network allowlist can expose the connection. Use the approved sources and test access from the reporting tool.
outcome: The reporting team can query the approved Workfront data through a tested connection.

steps: Agree the approved cost model, project examples and ownership with finance.
Configure the approved job role and user rates and test project cost calculations.
Reconcile the sample results with finance and document the rate maintenance process.
asks: Approved financial model and sample project records
risk: An incorrect rate can affect cost reporting. Reconcile sample calculations before teams use the new rates.
outcome: Finance and project owners can verify planned and actual costs in Workfront against the approved model.
